summary: Reviewed the reconciliation (criteria 9-13) against the diff: behavior is correct and complete on all 13 criteria and every gate passes, but two test-quality findings need refine — one loop-bound test is vacuous (passes with the escalation deleted) and the coherence chain's awaiting_human=>need_more_info link is asserted only as a tautology.

details.verdict: correct and complete; no behavior defects; 2 test-quality findings for refine

gates_run_by_me.lint: pass (biome + tsc + knip + madge, no circular deps)

findings.test: cannot re-form the loop — once escalated, the task leaves the poll set and a later poll does nothing
findings.summary: The test mocks getBlockedTasksByReason to return [] and then polls ONCE, so poll() exits at the empty-task-list guard (pr-event-poller.ts:63-66) before reaching any escalation code. The approve()/merge_state:blocked fixtures are never consulted and both assertions are trivially true. It passes with the entire escalation feature deleted — a dead guard sitting on acceptance criterion 3 (the unbounded pr_ready_to_merge re-entry path), the issue's headline invariant.
findings.behavior_impact: none — the bound is structural (need_more_info != pr_review_pending) and the sibling test asserts the written reason; this is false confidence, not a live bug
findings.fix: Make it a genuine two-poll test: poll once (assert exactly one `blocked` write), then mockReturnValue([]) for the second call, poll again, and assert no second block write and no requestTransition. Stronger: have setup's getBlockedTasksByReason fake filter on the blocked.reason the poller actually wrote, so the test proves the write is what removes the task from the poll set.

findings.summary: `expect(HOST_BLOCKED_MERGE_CATEGORY).toBe(BlockCategories.awaiting_human)` restates the constant's own definition — a tautology. Its comment claims it proves 'awaiting_human => need_more_info => off the poll set', but that derivation (via the unexported toBlockReason in orchestrator/index.ts:85-97) is never exercised. The poller path is covered (it writes need_more_info literally); the auto-merge path returns only a category, so if toBlockReason ever mapped awaiting_human -> pr_review_pending the loop would return with every test green. The plan explicitly called for this assertion (§32 Step 4) and it was dropped.
findings.behavior_impact: none — low likelihood (toBlockReason is shared by every needs_human block); this closes the one unasserted link in the coherence chain
findings.fix: Export toBlockReason from src/core/orchestrator/index.ts and assert toBlockReason(HOST_BLOCKED_MERGE_CATEGORY) === BlockReasons.need_more_info (and !== pr_review_pending). If exporting is unwanted, delete the tautology rather than keep a guard that cannot fail.

verified_not_defects: Deleting notifyHostBlockedMerge is sound: blockTask -> deliverBlockedQuestion (orchestrator/index.ts:456-476, outreach.ts:44-59) posts a ticket comment AND a chat question for an awaiting_human block, and auto-merge writes no outreach files so `needed` is the delivered text. No lost message, no double message.

The paths' differing notification kinds (poller `alert` vs block-delivery `question`) are NOT a criterion-9 gap: response-poller.ts:181 keys resumption on blocked.reason != pr_review_pending, not on the notification kind, so both paths are equally resumable.
All 4 merge_state consumers in src/ handle the new `blocked` value; no exhaustive switch broken; derivePrEvents withholds both pr_ready_to_merge and pr_merge_conflict for a blocked PR.

The new host-blocked-merge.ts file earns its keep despite being one const + one function: its two callers live in different layers (daemon vs pipeline), and message drift between two copies is how this bug was born.
details.ships_clean: 12 source/doc/test files, nothing else. Bundle regenerated from its markdown source (not hand-edited). No stray files, debug logging, .only/.skip, or dangling refs to the deleted notifyHostBlockedMerge.
